title: Morphisms, and hence the group law, descend
statement:
Let $X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes and let $V\to X$, $W\to X$ be schemes
with descent data over $X/Y$ which are
effective, with descended schemes $V_0,W_0$ over $Y$. Then every morphism
$\psi:V\to W$ over $X$ which is compatible with the two descent data descends
to a unique morphism $\psi_0:V_0\to W_0$ over $Y$.

proof.text: Use the effective descent projections and transport data of [def-pd-descent-datum], with the pullback square of [def-pc-base-change]. Base-change stability gives Flat, Surjective and QuasiCompact for qV. Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.Fpqc supplies EffectiveEpi qV. For a,b:T→V with a≫qV=b≫qV, the pullback square implies equality of their composites to Y. Transport of a to the X-component of b equals b by the pullback universal property and hDV. Compatibility hψ and hEW then show a≫ψ≫qW=b≫ψ≫qW. EffectiveEpi.desc and EffectiveEpi.fac give a unique underlying map ψ₀:V₀→W₀. Cancelling the epi qV shows ψ₀ is over Y, and cancellation again gives uniqueness as an Over morphism. This proves full faithfulness under the unchanged Lean fpqc hypotheses.

proof_origin.place: fpqc EffectiveEpi instance and EffectiveEpi.desc/fac, applied to the base-change projection; T1 stage-3 proof
